pr.title: fix ensure_monomorphic_enough
pr.author: lukas-code

analysis.originalLogic: `ensure_monomorphic_enough` in `compiler/rustc_const_eval/src/interpret/util.rs` is the guard that stops const interpretation from producing values that still depend on uninstantiated generics. The intended/original invariant is: a type is monomorphic enough only if it contains no type or const parameters at all; otherwise const eval must throw `TooGeneric`. The post-fix implementation expresses this directly: `if ty.has_param() {` then `throw_inval!(TooGeneric);` followed by `interp_ok(())`. Previously (before polymorphization was removed) a visitor walked function/closure/coroutine types looking for `ty::Param`, but the intent was still to reject types parameterized by generics rather than silently interpreting them.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: After polymorphization removal, the visitor was changed to "always treat all parameters as polymorphic and never recurse into them": for `ty::Closure(..) | ty::CoroutineClosure(..) | ty::Coroutine(..) | ty::FnDef(..)` it returned `ControlFlow::Continue(())` without visiting the type's substs, and for other kinds it used `super_visit_with`. Consequently a `FnDef` such as `generic::<T>` passed the outer `if !ty.has_param()` check, but the visitor never reached the nested `T`, so no `ty::Param` was found and `ensure_monomorphic_enough` returned `interp_ok(())` instead of `TooGeneric`. Const eval could then evaluate `std::intrinsics::type_id` for the still-generic function item, yielding a concrete constant, and GVN folded the comparison `Eq(const cursed_is_i32::<T>::{constant#0}, const cursed_is_i32::<T>::{constant#1})` into a fixed boolean (the report says release mode prints `false`). The corrected transformation keeps the comparison and its generic constants unevaluated, as shown by the expected MIR `_0 = Eq(const cursed_is_i32::<T>::{constant#0}, const cursed_is_i32::<T>::{constant#1});` both before and after GVN.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions generic over a type parameter `T: 'static`, containing const blocks that call `std::intrinsics::type_id::<T>()` (or another const-eval intrinsic) on a generic item such as `generic::<T>` and on a concrete instantiation such as `generic::<i32>`, compiled with `-C opt-level=2` so that MIR GVN runs. The compared values are constants whose identities depend on whether the generic parameter is instantiated.
analysis.summary: Bug fix: const-eval's `ensure_monomorphic_enough` stopped rejecting types that only contained generic parameters nested inside `FnDef`/closure/coroutine substs. A `generic::<T>` function item was therefore treated as monomorphic enough, `type_id` was evaluated with an uninstantiated `T`, and GVN folded the resulting constant comparison to a fixed boolean (reported as `false` in release). The fix reverts to throwing `TooGeneric` whenever the type has any parameter, keeping the comparison as `Eq(const ...<T>..., const ...<T>...)`; the new MIR regression test asserts that GVN does not fold it.
analysis.trigger: Const eval needs to interpret `type_id` for a type that contains a generic parameter only underneath a `FnDef`/`Closure`/`Coroutine`/`CoroutineClosure` (e.g. `generic::<T>`), and then GVN sees an `Eq` of two constants derived from those evaluations.
preconditions: The enclosing function is generic, e.g. `fn cursed_is_i32<T: 'static>() -> bool`.
The const expression depends on a generic parameter via `std::intrinsics::type_id::<T>()` or equivalent.
The generic parameter is nested inside a function item/closure/coroutine type (`generic::<T>`) rather than appearing as a direct `ty::Param`.
pitfalls: Do not attribute the root cause to GVN itself: the bad value originates in const eval deciding `generic::<T>` was monomorphic enough because the visitor skipped FnDef/Closure substs; GVN only folds the resulting bogus constant comparison.
Do not expect the corrected MIR to evaluate/fold the comparison; the fix intentionally leaves `Eq(const ...<T>...)` in place because the constants are too generic.

Do not treat the outer `ty.has_param()` check as sufficient when a visitor is used: `has_param()` is true for `FnDef` substs, but a visitor that does not recurse into `FnDef` substs will miss the nested `ty::Param`.
The added `.diff` file shows identical before/after GVN MIR; that is the expected corrected behavior, not evidence that the test is vacuous or that a replacement pass changed output.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR-opt regression test using `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and `//@ compile-flags: -C opt-level=2`, with `#![feature(core_intrinsics)]`, a `fn generic<T>() {}`, a `const fn type_id_of_val<T: 'static>(_: &T) -> u128` calling `std::intrinsics::type_id::<T>()`, and a generic `cursed_is_i32<T: 'static>()` comparing `type_id_of_val(&generic::<T>)` with `type_id_of_val(&generic::<i32>)`. Emit MIR and check that GVN leaves the comparison: `// CHECK: _0 = Eq(const cursed_is_i32::<T>::{constant#0}, const cursed_is_i32::<T>::{constant#1});` followed by `// CHECK-NEXT: return;`, i.e. it must not be folded to a constant boolean. The test file `tests/mir-opt/gvn_type_id_polymorphic.rs` and its `.diff` use exactly this shape.
evidence: When polymorphization got removed, this got changed to always treat all parameters as polymorphic and never recurse into them
This is clearly wrong and can cause MIR opts to misbehave, for example this currently prints "false" in release mode:
This PR reverts to the old behavior of always treating all types that contain type parameters as too generic, like we used to do without `-Zpolymorphize` before.
